notes.title: UPDATE 1.0.9 IS LIVE!
notes.content:
Hey fighters!

Update 1.0.9 is here! Here are the detailed notes:


- It is no longer possible to change active stance during an attack, even for S2 and S3.
- The perfect parry with the wakizashi was resetting too soon, making it impossible to block S3 attacks. This has been fixed.
- Feint locking is fixed. Previously, it was possible to execute a feint over and over, entering a state of constant attack -> feint -> attack loop, which was very hard to defend against. Not anymore.
- Some Nodachi attacks don't play feint animations at the end anymore.
- It is no longer possible to open the pause menu when the app loses focus during travel to character selection from the waiting room. 
- Duel history records have been added to the Stats screen.

Keep it up fighters! See you on Discord!

notes.title: Rating System Overhaul
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/db5cee9c095a5678ab7e80df58603bafc818116e.jpg[/img]

Hey fighters! ⚔️

"Our newest update, [b]1.0.5,[/b] among many other changes, also aims to bring more accuracy and fairness to how player skills are assessed and ranked. Here’s a detailed breakdown of the changes to the rating system:"

[list]
[*] [b]Accuracy-Based Rating:[/b] Player rating now incorporates an "accuracy" metric, which increases with the number of games played in ranked modes and decreases over time.
[*] [b]Impact on Ratings:[/b] Due to this new system, player ratings will initially decrease for everyone after this update.
[*] [b]Live Rating:[/b] A new stat called "Live Rating" has been introduced in the backend. This time-adjusted rating will be accessible in the next update. Live Rating reflects your rating decreased by the duration since your last game.
[*] [b]Rating Display:[/b] The game uses recorded ratings for leaderboards and player stat screens. After each match, your rating is recalculated, which may result in a decrease even if you win. This is expected and is due to the difference between "Live" and "Saved" ratings, as the game readjusts accuracy.
[/list]

In addition to this significant change, today's update brings many other changes, which can be found in the patch notes ⬇️

⚙️UPDATE 1.0.5. PATCH NOTES⚙️

- Combo system overhaul - Removed movement direction from all combos
- Perfect parry now affects attacker's stamina as well
- Reimplemented lighting for multiple levels. This should also increase readability of characters a bit.
- Fixed issue with leaderboard not showing the proper kill count
- S2 Attacks are now blockable
- Roll attack is now a bit faster - since it's S2 as well, it is now blockable
- Parry time is now increased to make it easier to perform in high ping scenarios
- Players can no longer move when parrying
- S3 attacks are no longer effective in tracking the enemy - can be countered by dash/rolls
- Stances can now be mapped to key/input - this should allow support for any (non-axial) input method
- Attack type as well as attack time are indicated using lens flare effects -
white = attack can be blocked, red = attack can't be blocked
- Players with more uncertain ratings (new players) will have lower ratings
- Added open-Discord button to the main menu

notes.title: UPDATE 1.0.4
notes.content:
[b]Hey Warriors![/b]

We are working hard to implement your feedback as quickly as possible. Therefore, we are pleased to bring you a new update, version 1.0.4, which includes the following changes to Die by the Blade:

[list]
[*] Added "open combo" mode for free flow sequences. This also means that roll attack is no longer predetermined and uses S2 attack of given stance - only allowed in local, hosted and practice modes. If community finds this as preferred system, then it will replace default combo system.
[*] Roll combo can now be executed only in MID stance (in default combo mode) - This should eliminate situations where players were able to change stances during roll.
[*] Forward roll and Backward roll are bit slower now.
[*] Fixed death animations with dismemberment. Characters no longer limp without limbs, but fall to the ground.
[*] Increased maximum distance of camera to fix characters being off the screen in certain situations. This can still happen, but should be less prominent now.
[*] Player rating is visible in stats and also with his name in online modes.
[*] Movement and attack speed are now properly affecting characters.
[*] Characters were rebalanced for specific attribute or attribute combination.
[*] Server location info is now present in overlay.
[*] Added sanity check and update of Mouse sensitivity setting when the game starts.
[*] Added option to enable/disable depletable stamina in practice mode.
[*] Added option to turn ON/OFF haptic feedback for controllers.
[*] Added note to online lobbies that rating will be updated only when playing ranked online modes.
[*] Updated icon for Rating stat.
[*] Increased katana stagger state length after parry.
[*] Parry takes less time to recover from.
[*] Rolls and dashes are now using more resolve and can't be executed if resolve is too low.
[*] Increased warm-up frame count and active frame count in Chokuto top stance attack. It should be easier to parry/block it now.
[*] Fixed issue with mouse input not registered for some players. If problem persists, please switch game to fullscreen mode. Then you can go back to borderless and it will work. New installs will run the game in fullscreen by default.
[*] Fixed issue on character selection screen with some equipments being rendered with low-res textures.
[*] Fixed animation issue with LOW-VERTICAL chokuto attack which was not registering hit.
[*] In finisher tutorial, player no longer resets when hitting opponent with S1 or S2, making it easier to execute.
[*] Fixed several issues in Chinese, Korean, German, Spanish and Japanese localization.
[/list]

notes.title: Die by the Blade is coming to PC in May with consoles to follow in October!
notes.content:
[h1]Hey Warriors! [/h1]

Hope this message finds you in good spirits! We've got some important news to share about Die by the Blade.

After a serious consideration, we mutually agreed to [b]part ways with our publishing partner.[/b] It was a difficult decision for everyone to make but it is in the best interest of our game and its future.

We're very sorry for the extended wait for our game, and for the silence. We heard your shouts and concerns, but we were engaged in long and complicated negotiations to acquire the project back from our publishing partner and at the same time to secure an investor to finalize the game. It was frustrating to not be able to share the progress of the complicated situation with you –  confidentiality and the idea of jinxing the success kept us on the down-low - but from now on, we can finally talk openly and we will share all with you until the launch!

The cool part? No more delays and full steam to the launch! We're dropping Die by the Blade on PC first on [b]16.05.2024[/b] followed by [b]XBOX and Playstation versions in October.[/b] We put all the efforts to meet your expectations and make Die by the Blade the great game we’ve promised and you supported!

We want to chat with you, hear your thoughts, and answer your questions. Hit us up on socials, forums, wherever you hang out. Your input is the most important to us.

Thanks for being the heartbeat of Die by the Blade. This journey's been wild, but we are in the finals now! Sharpen your swords and let's see how many will Die by the Blade this year!

notes.title: 🗡️ Choose Your Weapon: Nodachi Edition 🗡️
notes.content:
[h3]If you want to really test your upper body strength, the nodachi may be the weapon for you 💪[/h3]

In the latest instalment of our series on the weapons of Die by the Blade, we’re going to be looking at one of the largest weapons in the game, the mighty nodachi 😤

[previewyoutube=8RvG0xLpZBQ;full][/previewyoutube]

So what exactly is a nodachi?

[h3]What It Is[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/557a907cf303969b4197c12df01a0f4f1054a298.gif[/img]

Also known as the ōdachi, the nodachi is a long sword that was once used by samurai in feudal Japan. Its colossal size is even reflected in its name, as the first character of ō (大) literally translates to mean “big” or “great.” 

So how long exactly is this great sword? 

Although there is no exact definition of how long a nodachi needs to be, the blade is usually around 91 centimetres (36 in). To put that into perspective, that’s roughly the same length as the average car door!

[h3]Where It Came From[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/36ff2f1b45ea7065b2f5650f11d9379a1be1fccc.png[/img]

Use of the nodachi became popularised during the Kamakura period (1185－1333). This was largely due to the fact that battles on horseback were gradually becoming less common and were replaced by group battles, where the importance of foot soldiers was paramount. For the many warriors who did not have a horse and weren’t trained with a bow, there was a dire need for a powerful weapon they could yield in battle. Alongside being an effective way to fell your enemy, the size of the nodachi meant that it also served as an indicator of the warrior’s strength.

As time went on, however, the sheer length of the nodachi made it less and less effective on the battlefield, so it instead found a home within the shrine. Throughout its history, it was often used as an offering to divine spirits known as kami at Shinto shrines. By the Edo period (1603-1867), its existence on the battlefield was but a memory, and it was solely used as a religious offering. 

[h3]In Popular Culture[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/0cbeda4ce922103120909d1acfb2910b372f850c.png[/img]

Much like the wakizashi, the nodachi rarely appears in film or television outside of Japanese films about samurai 🗡️

The most prominent example is the Akira Kurosawa classic [i]Seven Samurai[/i], where the character Kikuchiyo wields a nodachi that is nearly as big as he is!

Would you be willing to sacrifice speed for the power of larger weapons like the nodachi? Or do you prefer short and swift blades like the wakizashi? 🤺

Let us know in the comments 💬

notes.title: 🗡️ Choose Your Weapon: Wakizashi Edition 🗡️
notes.content:
What could possibly be better than one sword? 🤔

Two swords, of course!

In the latest instalment of our series on the weapons of Die by the Blade, we’re going to be taking a closer look at the wakizashi ⚔️

[previewyoutube=UO7zRhtmq1w;full][/previewyoutube]

So what exactly is a wakizashi?

[h2]What It Is[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/3b114eae78afcb989404f86af083068db6585a56.gif[/img]

A wakizashi is a Japanese sword with a curved, single-edged blade that typically measures between 30 to 60 centimetres (12 to 24 in) in length. Its name translates to mean “side-inserted sword” in reference to the fact that it would be worn on the side of the body through a sash known as an obi. It’s important to note that wakizashi were not just smaller versions of the katana and could even be the same length!

[h2]Where It Came From[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/3734eb150c5a65fe1219ade272c18f769695678b.png[/img]

The wakizashi has been used in Japan from as far back as the 15th century, but became particularly popular during the Edo period (1603-1867), when the Tokugawa shogunate made it a requirement for samurai to wear a shorter sword alongside their katana. In fact, during this time, having a katana paired with a wakizashi became the official sign that the wearer was a samurai!

When worn together with a katana, the combination was known as daishō, meaning “big-little.” Only samurai were permitted to wear the daishō pairing, so it served as a symbol of their social status. When paired like this, the wakizashi was used as a back-up sword, but could also be useful in close quarters combat, to behead a defeated opponent, or to commit seppuku.  

[h2]In Popular Culture[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/18b509cc63fe6c3177fb18988a6a4dc94e4cdc73.png[/img]

In terms of popular culture, the wakizashi is nowhere near as widespread as the katana 🗡️

It has mainly featured in Japanese films about samurai, such as [i]Samurai II: Duel at Ichijoji Temple[/i], [i]Chikemuri Takadanobaba[/i], and [i]13 Assassins[/i]. 

Are you a fan of dual-wielding? Or do you prefer to master a single deadly weapon?

notes.title: 🗡️ Choose Your Weapon: Katana Edition 🗡️
notes.content:
A warrior would be nothing without their weapon, which is why we’ll be doing a series of deep dives into the traditional Japanese weapons that will feature in Die by the Blade!

To kick off our “Choose Your Weapon” series, we’ll be taking a closer look at one of the core weapons in the game: the katana. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/ea6ad09eb1ab7f22663171143ec1453a98b97941.gif[/img]


To start off, what exactly is a katana?

[h2]What It Is[/h2]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/bf531aab75eaf008f48a5eae468dce25a74efb63.gif[/img]


A katana is a Japanese sword with a curved, single-edged blade and a circular or squared guard. Its long grip is designed so that it can comfortably be held with two hands. While people around the world will be familiar with the katana almost immediately thanks to its role in popular culture, in Japan this type of sword is officially known as an uchigatana, with the word katana more often being used to refer to any type of single-edged sword from around the world!

[h2]Where It Came From[/h2]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/f092e77d2fb2e61aebfd1391ecf18e52dc67b8dd.png[/img]


The use of longer weapons such as the katana became commonplace in feudal Japan towards the beginning of the Muromachi period (1336-1573). Unlike the tachi, which had been the weapon of choice for samurai of the past, the katana was worn in a belt-like sash known as an obi with the sharpened edge facing up, rather than facing down. This meant that a well-trained samurai could draw their sword and strike a killing blow all in one single motion 💀

Throughout Japanese history, the role of the katana changed, from a deadly weapon to a work of art. Sword fittings would be made with luxurious black lacquer and ornately inlaid with delicate etchings. To this day, the katana occupies a dual role in Japanese culture as both a powerful tool within martial arts and a ceremonial item of unparalleled beauty. 

[h2]In Popular Culture[/h2]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/c84e28ff113370fc7b2f9b90e490a33ed87d6a82.png[/img]


From comic books and anime to films and video games, the katana is by far the most widely known and featured amongst all traditional Japanese weapons 🗡️

Whether you were first introduced to the katana while watching Seven Samurai or it sliced its way into your life thanks to Leonardo from Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, chances are you’ve come across this noble blade. 

Who is your favourite katana-wielding character?

Let us know in the comments 💬

notes.title: Get Ready to Sleigh - A Pre-Christmas Update
notes.content:
We’d like to wish all of our followers a Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year. This year has been one of growth and achievement for us, so we’re more excited than ever to bring you brutal one-hit-kill action in the coming year. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/c0c16486d9f2191aec63551282bb7a3c17fff6b1.png[/img]

In the spirit of the season, we’ve got a special Christmas update for you. Watch the video below and enjoy a sneak peek at what we have been working on over the past year!

[previewyoutube=iiVvRHfYfEM;full][/previewyoutube]

[i]Die by the Blade[/i] will be releasing across all platforms in 2022, but what’s going to happen in the meantime? And how can you stay informed on the latest updates?

We’ve got a tonne of announcements planned for next year, including character reveals, new weapons, gameplay footage, and lots more!

If you want to keep up to date with our progress on the game and get to see the most recent gameplay footage, you can follow us on [url=https://www.facebook.com/dbtbgame]Facebook[/url], [url=https://twitter.com/dbtbgame]Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/dbtbgame/]Instagram[/url], or [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@dbtbgame]TikTok[/url]. We’ll be posting everything from behind the scenes footage to in-game screenshots, so you won’t want to miss it!

For now, we’d like to say thank you to all of our followers for your ongoing support and feedback on [i]Die by the Blade[/i]. Don’t forget to wishlist [i]Die by the Blade[/i] on Steam if you haven’t already.

Let us eat cake!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35811916/89db58e5b1b6027b34861e00ce1cffde004f050d.png[/img]

notes.title: We're very excited to announce Kwalee as our new publishing partner!
notes.content:
[h2]Hey everyone![/h2]

We're super excited to announce our new publishing partner, Kwalee, who will be publishing Die by the Blade for release on Steam and Console platforms [b]next year[/b]!

We can't wait to share more details with you about the game as we move closer to the road to launch, with new content drops, reveals, trailers and more to be revealed soon.

Check out the Kwalee Announcement trailer below!

[previewyoutube=zqj4EHxmM3o;full][/previewyoutube]

We also have some exciting upcoming event plans (more on that next week!) so keep an eye on the Steam page for more updates.

Thank you all for your support and continued excitement for the game and we look forward to sharing more details soon, make sure to wishlist the game below for all the news drops!
